newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pacific BBA still sees flat 96 result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pacific BBA still sees flat 96 result.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific BBA Ltd managing director Barry Jackson on Tuesday reaffirmed his expectations that the group results for calendar 1996 would be similar to those a year earlier.
However, the 1997 results would be stronger, he told a Securities Institute of Australia presentation.
"The outlook for 1996 is still flat," Jackson said.
Pacific BBA reported a net profit of A$15.9 million in 1995.
Jackson said the group's automotive division had had a similar year to 1995, while margins in the troubled plastics division had contracted in the second half.
"We had a good first half (in plastics)," Jackson noted.
Despite the weakness in the second half, 1997 was expected to be a better year for the group, he said.
Jackson expected growth in export brake sales and continued growth in sales to the Asian region.
However, Australian operations would remain a challenge, he said. "The only question is what is going to happen in 1997 in Australia," he said.
Jackson said the company was still keen to make acquisitions but was finding it hard to locate companies that met Pacific BBA's criteria.
"They're hard to find...but we will find them," he said.
Pacific BBA in August failed in a cash and share bid for fellow manufactuer Azon Ltd, which was bought by U.S.-based Illinois Tool Works Inc.
